docs.title: DeNovoWEST
docs.text:
Beta documentation

This documentation describes DeNovoWEST 2.0.0-beta, developed on the develop branch. Options and output formats may still change before the 2.0.0 release. The method as published in 2020 is still available on the master branch for now.

DeNovoWEST (De Novo Weighted Enrichment Simulation Test) tests whether genes carry more damaging de novo mutations (DNMs) than expected by chance in a cohort of parent–offspring trios.

It combines two complementary gene-level tests:

  • an enrichment test, which compares the observed burden of DNMs in a gene, weighted by a variant severity score, against a gene-specific null distribution built from expected mutation rates;
  • a clustering test (via denovonear), which asks whether missense DNMs are more clustered than expected along the protein sequence or in its 3D structure.

The original method is described in Kaplanis, Samocha, Wiel, Zhang et al., Nature 2020.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
DeNovoWEST 2 is distributed as:

  • a Nextflow workflow (nextflow/) that runs the full analysis, from building a mutation rates file to producing gene-level p-values;
  • a Python package and command-line tool (denovowest) exposing the individual steps (annotation, enrichment simulation).
flowchart LR
    GFF[GFF + genome FASTA] --> R[Rates file creation]
    MM[Mutation rate model] --> R
    R --> AR[Rates annotation]
    DNM[Observed DNMs] --> F[DNM filtering] --> AD[DNM annotation]
    AR --> E[Enrichment test]
    AD --> E
    AR --> C[Clustering test]
    AD --> C
    E --> CMB[Combined p-values]
    C --> CMB
    %% CMB --> REP[HTML report]

docs.title: Getting help
docs.text: Please report bugs and ask questions on the GitHub issue tracker. If you use DeNovoWEST in your work, please cite it.

docs.title: Citation
docs.text:
If you use DeNovoWEST, please cite:

Kaplanis J, Samocha KE, Wiel L, Zhang Z, et al. Evidence for 28 genetic disorders discovered by combining healthcare and research data. Nature 586, 757–762 (2020). doi:10.1038/s41586-020-2832-5

@article{kaplanis2020,
  title   = {Evidence for 28 genetic disorders discovered by combining healthcare and research data},
  author  = {Kaplanis, Joanna and Samocha, Kaitlin E. and Wiel, Laurens and Zhang, Zhancheng and others},
  journal = {Nature},
  volume  = {586},
  pages   = {757--762},
  year    = {2020},
  doi     = {10.1038/s41586-020-2832-5}
}

Please also report the DeNovoWEST version you used, and cite the resources your analysis relies on, in particular the mutation rate model and the variant scores (see Resources).

If you use the clustering test, please also cite denovonear:

Deciphering Developmental Disorders Study. Prevalence and architecture of de novo mutations in developmental disorders. Nature 542, 433–438 (2017). doi:10.1038/nature21062

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
There are two ways to use DeNovoWEST:

  • the Nextflow workflow, recommended for full analyses: it handles splitting the work by gene, running steps in parallel and keeping track of outputs;
  • the Python command-line tool, to run a single step (e.g. annotate a file or run the enrichment test on files you prepared yourself).

docs.title: Get the code
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/HurlesGroupSanger/DeNovoWEST.git
cd DeNovoWEST
git checkout develop   # DeNovoWEST 2 is currently developed on this branch

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Tool Version Notes Nextflow ≥ 23.10 conda provides the Python environment for each process bcftools ≥ 1.19 used for consequence annotation (bcftools csq) tabix / bgzip (htslib) sorting and indexing rates files bedtools only when filtering excluded regions jq merging simulation logs

bcftools, tabix, bedtools and jq must be available on your PATH, or loaded through environment modules (see Using environment modules).

docs.title: Software environment
docs.text:
Nextflow builds the conda environment from misc/conda/denovowest.yml the first time the workflow runs; conf/local.conf already points to it. Enable conda in your configuration file:

conda.enabled = true

Tip

On a cluster, set conda.cacheDir (or the NXF_CONDA_CACHEDIR environment variable) to a shared location so the environment is only built once.

docs.title: Using environment modules
docs.text:
On HPC systems where bcftools, tabix and bedtools are provided as environment modules, add the module names to the params block of your configuration file instead of installing them:

params {
  useModules     = true
  bcftoolsModule = 'bcftools/1.20'
  tabixModule    = 'samtools/1.20'
  bedtoolsModule = 'bedtools/2.31'
}

Module names are site-specific; check module avail on your system.

docs.title: Python package
docs.text:
The denovowest package requires Python ≥ 3.10 and is published on PyPI.

Version numbers

The Python package has its own version number, separate from the version of DeNovoWEST (the method and workflow, currently 2.0.0-beta). The conda environment used by the workflow installs the package from PyPI.

From PyPIFrom a clone (development) 
pip install denovowest

pip install -e .

Changes to the source code then take effect without reinstalling. See Development.

Check the installation:

denovowest --help

The clustering test relies on denovonear, which is installed by the conda environment. Install it separately (pip install denovonear) if you use the Python package on its own and want to run clustering.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Run the quick start to check that everything works.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: This page runs the whole workflow on a toy dataset: a single gene (OR4F5) and a handful of DNMs bundled with the repository. It takes a few minutes and is the best way to check your installation.

docs.title: Run the toy example
docs.text:
cd DeNovoWEST/nextflow
nextflow run denovowest.nf -c nextflow.config.full

nextflow.config.full switches on every step:

  1. build a mutation rates file for OR4F5 with the trinucleotide (kmer) model;
  2. annotate the rates and the DNMs with their consequence (bcftools csq) and a CADD score;
  3. run the enrichment test on all coding variants and on missense variants;
  4. run the linear clustering test;
  5. combine enrichment and clustering p-values.

Environment modules

The example configuration files load bcftools and tabix through environment modules with Sanger-specific module names (useModules = true). If these tools are on your PATH, set useModules = false; otherwise change the module names. See Using environment modules.

docs.title: Look at the results
docs.text:
Results are written to nextflow/test/out/full/:

test/out/full/
├── configs/                 copy of the configuration used, with the git commit
├── rates/                   mutation rates file, annotated and indexed
├── dnm/                     DNMs kept / discarded by filtering, and annotated DNMs
├── simulation/
│   ├── all-coding/          enrichment test on all coding variants
│   └── mis/                 enrichment test on missense variants
├── clustering/linear/       clustering test results
└── combined_tests/          final per-gene p-values

The file most people want is combined_tests/combined_tests_results.tsv, with one row per gene and its minimum p-value across tests. All files are described in Output files.

Nextflow's intermediate files go to test/work/full/, and execution reports (timeline, resource usage) to test/trace/full/.

docs.title: Other example configurations
docs.text:
nextflow/ holds one example configuration per typical use. Copy one and adapt it for your data:

File What it runs nextflow.config.annotate create and annotate a rates file, annotate DNMs nextflow.config.enrichment enrichment test from already annotated rates and DNM files nextflow.config.clustering clustering test from already annotated rates and DNM files nextflow.config.full everything above in one run

docs.title: What's new in DeNovoWEST 2
docs.text:
DeNovoWEST 2 is a rewrite of the code used in the 2020 publication. The statistical approach is the same; what changed is how the inputs are produced, how variants are scored, and how the analysis is run.

The 2020 code remains available on the v1.0.0 branch.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• A complete workflow. v1 needed a pre-computed rates file and scripts submitted by hand. v2 builds the rates file, annotates it, filters and annotates the DNMs, and runs both tests in one Nextflow workflow.
  • Any variant score. v1 used PPV weights estimated from CADD, shet and missense constraint in the DDD cohort. v2 uses any numerical score from the rates and DNM files (CADD, AlphaMissense, REVEL, popEVE…), with possibly a different score for the missense test.
  • Several mutation rate models: trinucleotide context, Roulette and Carlson.
  • Integrated clustering test, in linear or 3D protein space.
  • New options: excluded regions, adjustment for positive selection in sperm, imputation of missing scores, new run types (syn, ptv, protein-altering).
  • Quality control: mutation rate statistics, O/E ratios.

docs.title: Configuration reference
docs.text:
The workflow is configured with a Nextflow configuration file passed with -c:

nextflow run denovowest.nf -c my_analysis.config

Start from one of the example files in nextflow/ (see Quick start). The workflow prints all the parameters it received when it starts, and saves a copy of the configuration file in the output directory at the end of the run.

docs.title: Structure of a configuration file
docs.text:
includeConfig 'conf/local.conf'     // or conf/lsf.conf, see "Running on a cluster"
includeConfig 'conf/default.conf'

conda.enabled = true

params.basedir  = "/path/to/analyses"
params.run_name = "kmer_cadd"

workDir       = "${params.basedir}/work/${params.run_name}"
params.outdir = "${params.basedir}/out/${params.run_name}"

params {
  // 1. modes: which steps to run
  // 2. shared parameters: input files used by several steps
  // 3. one block per step: rates_creation { }, annotation { }, enrichment { }, clustering { }
}

Tip

Keep the same basedir for a project and change only run_name between analyses (e.g. kmer vs roulette mutation rate model). Each run then gets its own output and work directory.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
Steps are switched on with boolean flags in params. They are all false by default, and at least one must be set.

Parameter Runs create_rates Rates file creation from the GFF and a mutation rate model annotate_rates Annotation of the rates file annotate_dnm Annotation of the DNM file run_enrichment Enrichment test run_clustering Clustering test plot_oe_ratios Observed / expected ratio QC

Steps can be combined in a single run (e.g. nextflow.config.full) or run separately, feeding the outputs of one run to the next (e.g. annotate once, then try several enrichment settings).

When both enrichment (with runtype = "both") and clustering are switched on, the workflow also combines their p-values (see Output files).

docs.title: Shared parameters
docs.text:
Set at the top level of params.

Parameter Type Default Description dnm path — Observed DNM file. See Input files. rates path — An existing rates file (bgzipped, with a .tbi index). When set, create_rates is skipped. gff path — Gene annotation in GFF3 format. Required to create or annotate rates, annotate DNMs, and for clustering. genome_fasta path — Reference genome FASTA, with a .fai index next to it. gene_list path — Restrict the analysis to these genes (one gene_id per line, as in the GFF, version included). If not set, the list is taken from the rates file, or from the GFF. excluded_regions path — BED file of regions to remove from both the rates and the DNM files (e.g. low-complexity regions, segmental duplications). exclude_sex_chromosomes bool false Discard DNMs on chromosomes X and Y. sperm_positive_selection_adjustment path — JSON file of factors used to scale mutation rates for genes or sites under positive selection in the male germline. See Mutation rates. split_step int 100 Number of genes per batch. Each batch is processed as a separate job. gff_db path — A gffutils database already built from gff, to skip rebuilding it. Mostly useful for development and tests.

docs.title: Tools from environment modules
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description useModules bool false Load tools with module load before the processes that need them. bcftoolsModule str — Module providing bcftools ≥ 1.19. tabixModule str — Module providing tabix and bgzip. bedtoolsModule str — Module providing bedtools (only needed with excluded_regions).

docs.title: Rates file creation (rates_creation)
docs.text:
Used when create_rates = true and no rates file is given. A rates file lists every possible single-nucleotide substitution in the coding sequence and splice regions of each gene, with its expected mutation rate. See Mutation rates.

Parameter Type Allowed values Default Description model str kmer, roulette, carlson kmer Mutation rate model. path path — — Model data: a trinucleotide rates table for kmer (e.g. resources/rates_model_dnn.tsv), or the directory of per-chromosome VCFs for roulette and carlson. scaling_factor float — — Factor by which roulette and carlson rates are multiplied to obtain per-generation, per-haploid-genome probabilities. Required for these two models. See Mutation rates. 
rates_creation {
  model = "roulette"
  path = "/data/roulette/"
  scaling_factor = 5.075e-8   // Roulette default, see Mutation rates
}

docs.title: Annotation (annotation)
docs.text:
Used when annotate_rates and/or annotate_dnm is set. The rates file and the DNM file are annotated with the same sources, so that any annotation can later be used as the score in the enrichment test. Each source is optional.

Parameter Type Default Description annotate_bcftoolscsq bool true Annotate the consequence of each variant (e.g. missense_variant, stop_gained) with bcftools csq and the gff file. The enrichment test needs a consequence column. cadd_file path — CADD scores (tabix-indexed TSV). Adds the columns raw and score (PHRED-scaled). dbnsfp map — Scores from dbNSFP, see below. custom map — Columns from up to three tab-separated, tabix-indexed files, see below. vcf map — Fields from the INFO column of up to three VCF files, see below.

The formats of these files are described in Input files.

Contig names

CADD, dbNSFP, custom and VCF annotation files must name chromosomes without the chr prefix (1, not chr1), as distributed by CADD and dbNSFP. The prefix of the rates and DNM files does not matter.

docs.title: dbNSFP, custom and VCF sources
docs.text:
These sources accept a list of columns to extract. Give it either inline (columns, comma-separated) or in a file with one column name per line (columns_file). If neither is given, all columns are extracted.

Parameter Description dbnsfp.database Path to the genome-wide dbNSFP file (bgzipped, with .tbi). dbnsfp.columns / dbnsfp.columns_file dbNSFP columns to extract. custom.<name>.path Path to a tabix-indexed TSV whose first columns are chrom, pos, ref, alt. custom.<name>.columns / custom.<name>.columns_file Columns to extract. vcf.<name>.path Path to a bgzipped, tabix-indexed VCF. vcf.<name>.columns / vcf.<name>.columns_file INFO fields to extract.

<name> is a label of your choice. At most three custom and three vcf sources can be used in one run.

annotation {
  cadd_file = "/data/cadd/whole_genome_SNVs.tsv.gz"

  dbnsfp = [
    database: "/data/dbNSFP5.3.1a_grch38.gz",
    columns: "AlphaMissense_score,REVEL_score"
  ]

  custom = [
    "itan": [
      "path": "Itan_missense_full_annotations.tsv.gz",
      "columns_file": "Itan_annotations_to_keep.csv"
    ]
  ]

  vcf = [
    "cosmic": [
      "path": "Cosmic_GenomeScreensMutant_Normal_v101_GRCh38.vcf.gz",
      "columns": "GENOME_SCREEN_SAMPLE_COUNT"
    ],
    "popeve": [
      "path": "popevemap.vcf.gz",
      "columns": "popEVE,EVE,ESM1v"
    ]
  ]
}

docs.title: Enrichment test (enrichment)
docs.text:
Used when run_enrichment = true. Requires an annotated rates file and DNM file, either produced in the same run or given with rates and dnm. See Enrichment test.

Parameter Type Allowed values Default Description nmales int — required Number of male individuals in the cohort. nfemales int — required Number of female individuals in the cohort. score str or list — required Column of the rates and DNM files holding the variant severity score. With runtype = "both", a list of two columns [all_coding_score, missense_score] uses a different score for each test. runtype str all-coding, mis, both all-coding Test all coding and splice variants, missense variants only, or run both tests. See Run types. nsim int — 10000000 Number of simulations for each number of DNMs considered in a gene (see Enrichment test). impute_missing_scores bool — false Replace missing scores by the median score of the possible variants with the same consequence in the same gene, instead of discarding them. See Missing scores. cpus int — 1 Number of CPUs used by each enrichment job. debug bool — false Write detailed per-gene logs and use a fixed random seed, so that results are reproducible (with cpus = 1). 
enrichment {
  nmales = 17422
  nfemales = 13636
  score = ["CADD_phred", "AlphaMissense_score"]
  runtype = "both"
}

Note

The CLI also offers syn, ptv and protein-altering run types and lets you tune how indels are scored. These options are not yet exposed in the workflow; use denovowest simulation directly.

docs.title: Clustering test (clustering)
docs.text:
Used when run_clustering = true. Requires a DNM file and gff. See Clustering test.

Parameter Type Allowed values Default Description runtype str linear, 3D, both 3D Test clustering along the protein sequence, in the 3D protein structure, or both. protein_structures path — — Archive of AlphaFold predicted structures. Required for 3D and both. rates path — — Genome-wide mutation rates VCF (with .tbi) used by denovonear instead of its built-in model, e.g. Roulette rates, or the rates/rates_adjusted.vcf.gz file produced by the workflow.

docs.title: Observed / expected ratios (oe_ratios)
docs.text:
Used when plot_oe_ratios = true. Compares the number of observed DNMs with the number expected from the rates file, per consequence, as a quality check of the mutation rate model. Uses enrichment.nmales and enrichment.nfemales.

Parameter Type Default Description gene_categories path — Optional table assigning genes to categories; ratios are also computed per category. gnomad_constraints path — Optional gnomAD constraint table; ratios are also computed per LOEUF and missense constraint bin.

docs.title: Nextflow settings
docs.text:
The example configuration files also set:

  • workDir: where Nextflow keeps intermediate files. Use a scratch file system and delete it once a run is finished.
  • timeline and report: Nextflow execution reports, written to ${basedir}/trace/${run_name}/.

Use -resume to restart a run without recomputing completed steps:

nextflow run denovowest.nf -c my_analysis.config -resume

docs.title: Running on a cluster
docs.text: A full analysis of ~20,000 genes runs a few hundred jobs, some of them long, so it is usually run on a compute cluster. Nextflow submits the jobs for you: you only need to tell it which scheduler to use and how many resources each job needs.

docs.title: Execution profiles
docs.text:
The workflow ships with two profiles in nextflow/conf/. Include one at the top of your configuration file:

File Use conf/local.conf Run all jobs on the current machine. conf/lsf.conf Submit jobs to an LSF cluster. Written for the Wellcome Sanger Institute farm. 
includeConfig 'conf/lsf.conf'
includeConfig 'conf/default.conf'

docs.title: Adapting lsf.conf
docs.text:
lsf.conf defines resources per type of job:

Jobs Queue Memory Time default normal 2 GB 10 h process_long (enrichment and clustering) long 2 GB 48 h intensive (rates statistics) long 40 GB 48 h

Failed jobs are retried up to twice with more memory and time when they were killed for exceeding their limits.

Before using it outside the Sanger farm, edit:

  • the group passed to LSF in clusterOptions (-G team29-grp) — replace it with your own group (-G) or project (-P);
  • the queue names and the limits in the check_max function at the end of the file.

For other schedulers (Slurm, SGE, PBS…), copy lsf.conf, change executor and the clusterOptions, and see the Nextflow executor documentation.

docs.title: Running the workflow itself
docs.text:
The Nextflow process must keep running for the whole analysis, which can take days. Submit it as a job of its own, or run it inside screen / tmux on a login node if your site allows it:

bsub -q long -R "select[mem>4000] rusage[mem=4000]" -M 4000 \
     -o nextflow.%J.out -e nextflow.%J.err \
     "nextflow run denovowest.nf -c my_analysis.config -resume"

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
• split_step sets how many genes go in each job (default 100). Smaller batches mean more, shorter jobs.
  • enrichment.cpus sets the number of cores per enrichment job.
  • enrichment.nsim: the default of 107 simulations is needed to reach p-values small enough to pass exome-wide significance. Use far fewer (e.g. 104) when testing a configuration.
  • Put workDir on a fast scratch file system: it receives large intermediate files.

docs.title: Genomics England Research Environment
docs.text:
A few changes are needed to run on the Genomics England (GEL) HPC:

  • Conda channels must go through the GEL mirror: in misc/conda/denovowest.yml, prefix the channels with conda-:

    channels:
  - conda-conda-forge
  - conda-bioconda

  • bcftools ≥ 1.19 must be available.

  • LSF: in lsf.conf, use your project code in clusterOptions (-P <project>) and set queue = 'short' in the process block.
  • Nextflow ≥ 22 requires conda.enabled = true in the configuration file.

docs.title: Input files
docs.text:
All examples on this page come from the examples/ directory of the repository.

Conventions

  • Genome build: DeNovoWEST 2 is developed and tested on GRCh38.
  • Coordinates: 1-based, as in VCF files, with indels left-anchored (e.g. TC → T). BED files are 0-based, as usual.
  • Chromosome names: the DNM file, the rates file, the excluded regions and the genome FASTA must all use the same naming as the GFF (chr1 or 1).
  • Gene identifiers: the ID of the gene in the GFF, version included (e.g. ENSG00000186092.7).

docs.title: DNM file
docs.text:
Tab-separated text file with a header, one row per DNM (and per gene, if a DNM overlaps several genes).

Column Required Description gene_id yes, first column Gene identifier, as in the GFF. chrom yes, second column Chromosome. pos yes, third column Position (1-based). ref yes Reference allele. alt yes Alternative allele. consequence for the tests Added by the workflow when annotate_dnm is set (see Consequences). score columns for the enrichment test Added by the workflow from the annotation sources. any other column no Kept as is (e.g. gene_symbol, sample identifier). 
gene_id chrom   pos ref alt varid   gene_symbol
ENSG00000186092.7   chr1    65518   A   T   var_1   OR4F5
ENSG00000186092.7   chr1    65549   G   T   var_2   OR4F5

If your DNMs are not yet assigned to genes, misc/map_dnm_to_genes.py assigns each DNM to the genes of a GFF that it overlaps.

docs.title: Filtering
docs.text:
Before annotation, the workflow removes DNMs that:

  • have no gene_id;
  • are in a gene that is not in the gene list (not_in_gene_list);
  • are on chromosome X or Y, if exclude_sex_chromosomes = true (allosome);
  • do not overlap the coding sequence of their gene, extended by 8 bp on each side to include splice sites (not_in_cds, or gene_not_in_gff);
  • start in an excluded region (excluded_region).

Removed DNMs are written to dnm/dnms_discarded.tsv with the reason in the reason column (except those without gene_id).

docs.title: Rates file
docs.text:
Built by the workflow when create_rates = true. To reuse one, pass it with rates. See Mutation rates for how it is built.

One row per possible single-nucleotide substitution in the coding sequence of each gene, extended by 8 bp on each side.

Column Description gene_id, chrom, pos First three columns, in this order. ref, alt Alleles. prob Probability that this substitution arises de novo on one haploid genome in one generation. gene_symbol Gene name, if present in the GFF (gene_name attribute). consequence, full_consequence_bcftoolscsq Added by consequence annotation. score columns Added by the annotation sources. 
gene_id chrom   pos ref alt prob    consequence full_consequence_bcftoolscsq    raw score   transcript_in_dbnsfp    AlphaMissense_score
ENSG00000117139.19  chr1    202729039   C   A   1.164306866667408e-09   missense        2.672775    19.74   True    0.3881
ENSG00000117139.19  chr1    202729039   C   G   2.386829123982257e-09   missense        2.680624    19.77   True    0.3881

A rates file given with rates must be:

  • sorted by chrom, pos and alt;
  • compressed with bgzip and indexed with tabix -S 1 -s 2 -b 3 -e 3, with the index next to it (<rates>.tbi).

docs.title: GFF
docs.text:
A GFF3 file describing the genes to analyse, in the format expected by bcftools csq: gene features, transcripts as children of genes, and CDS features as children of transcripts.

Rates are built from every transcript of each gene in the GFF, so use a GFF with one transcript per gene, typically the MANE Select transcripts.

The following attributes are used:

Feature Attribute Use gene ID Gene identifier (gene_id everywhere). gene gene_name (or Name) Gene symbol. gene gene_id Matching of VCF annotations by gene. transcript transcript_id Matching of dbNSFP scores by transcript. 
chr1    HAVANA  gene    65419   71585   .   +   .   ID=ENSG00000186092.7;gene_id=ENSG00000186092.7;gene_type=protein_coding;gene_name=OR4F5;biotype=protein_coding;Name=OR4F5

GENCODE and Ensembl GFF3 files can be converted to the bcftools csq format with misc/gff2gff, from the bcftools repository:

zcat gencode.v49.basic.annotation.gff3.gz | misc/gff2gff | gzip -c > gencode.v49.bcftoolscsq.gff3.gz

docs.title: Genome FASTA
docs.text: The reference genome, with its index (samtools faidx) next to it as <genome_fasta>.fai. Chromosome names must match the GFF.

docs.title: Gene list
docs.text:
Plain text file, one gene identifier per line, no header:

ENSG00000186092.7

Identifiers must match the GFF ID, version included.

docs.title: Excluded regions
docs.text:
A BED file of regions to exclude, e.g. simple repeats, segmental duplications and the ENCODE blacklist. Variants in these regions are removed from the rates file and the DNM file, so that both are restricted to the same part of the genome.

chr1    0   10000
chr1    207666  257666

docs.title: Sperm positive selection adjustment
docs.text:
A JSON file of multipliers applied to the mutation rates of genes or sites under positive selection in the male germline. See Mutation rates.

{
  "genes": {
    "ENSG00000117139": { "missense": 4.88, "stop_gained": 27.92 }
  },
  "sites": {
    "chr12_112477719_A_G": {
      "chrom": "chr12", "pos": 112477719, "ref": "A", "alt": "G", "multiplier": 420.3
    }
  }
}
  • genes: for each gene (with or without version), a multiplier per consequence. The consequence must match the consequence column of the rates file, so the rates file must be annotated.
  • sites: a multiplier for a specific substitution. The key is free text; chrom must use the same naming as the rates file.

Both sections are optional, but at least one is required. A site in an adjusted gene gets both multipliers.

docs.title: Annotation sources
docs.text:
All sources must be compressed with bgzip and indexed with tabix (.tbi next to the file), and use chromosome names without the chr prefix. Annotations are matched on chromosome, position, reference and alternative allele.

If an annotation column has the same name as an existing column, it is renamed <column>_<source> (e.g. score_cadd). Missing values are written as ..

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
With annotation.annotate_bcftoolscsq = true (default), each variant is annotated with bcftools csq using the GFF. Two columns are added:

  • consequence: the most severe consequence of the variant on its own gene (e.g. missense, stop_gained, splice_donor, synonymous);
  • full_consequence_bcftoolscsq: the full combined consequence when it differs (e.g. missense&splice_region).

Consequences use the bcftools csq vocabulary. If you provide your own consequence column, it must use the same terms.

docs.title: CADD
docs.text:
The CADD whole-genome SNV file, e.g. whole_genome_SNVs.tsv.gz (CADD v1.7, GRCh38), with six columns: chromosome, position, reference, alternative, raw score, PHRED score.

#chrom  pos ref alt raw score
1   65419   C   A   1.159795    11.89

Adds the columns raw and score.

docs.title: dbNSFP
docs.text:
The genome-wide dbNSFP file for GRCh38 (tested with versions 5.2a and 5.3.1a). The header must include Ensembl_geneid and Ensembl_transcriptid.

When dbNSFP has several values for a variant (one per transcript), the maximum over the transcripts present in the GFF is kept, or else the maximum over the gene's transcripts. Adds the requested columns and transcript_in_dbnsfp.

docs.title: Custom TSV
docs.text: Any tab-separated file whose first four columns are chromosome, position, reference and alternative allele, with a header line (starting with # or not). Adds the requested columns, or all columns after the fourth.

docs.title: VCF
docs.text:
Any VCF file with annotations in the INFO column, e.g. popEVE or COSMIC. Adds the requested INFO fields, or all of them. Only the first alternative allele of each record is used.

#CHROM  POS ID  REF ALT QUAL    FILTER  INFO
1   65565   .   A   G   .   .   gene=OR4F5;popEVE=-4.754;EVE=10.471;ESM1v=-4.841

docs.title: O/E ratio inputs
docs.text: Parameter Format oe_ratios.gene_categories TSV with a header, gene_id in the first column (as in the rates file) and a category column. Genes absent from the file are grouped as not_in_user_gene_list. oe_ratios.gnomad_constraints The gnomAD v4.1 constraint_metrics.tsv file.

docs.title: Output files
docs.text:
All results are written under params.outdir. The layout below is for a full run; each directory only appears if the corresponding step ran.

<outdir>/
├── configs/
├── rates/
│   ├── stats/
│   └── split/
├── dnm/
├── simulation/
│   ├── all-coding/
│   └── mis/
├── clustering/
│   ├── linear/
│   ├── 3D/
│   └── combined/
├── combined_tests/
└── oe_ratios/

docs.title: configs/
docs.text: A copy of each configuration file used for the run, named <config file>.<YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM>. The git commit of DeNovoWEST used for the run is appended as the last line. Keep this file with your results: it is the record of how they were produced.

docs.title: rates/
docs.text: File When Description gene_list.tsv always Genes analysed. merged_rates.tsv.gz (+ .tbi) create_rates The rates file: every possible substitution in the analysed genes, with its mutation rate and, if annotate_rates is set, its annotations. This is the file to pass as rates to later runs. rates_adjusted.tsv.gz (+ .tbi) sperm_positive_selection_adjustment Rates file after adjustment for positive selection in sperm. rates_adjusted.vcf.gz (+ .tbi) annotate_rates The final rates file in VCF format, usable as clustering.rates. Named rates_adjusted even when no adjustment was applied. split/ create_rates Unannotated rates for each batch of genes (symbolic links to the work directory). stats/rates_stats.json rates file annotated or provided Summary statistics of the rates file, including the fraction of variants with missing annotations. stats/filtered_rates_stats.json excluded_regions Number of loci removed by region filtering, overall and per gene. stats/adjusted_rates.json sperm_positive_selection_adjustment Per-gene mutation rates before and after adjustment. stats/rates_per_gene_per_csq.tsv, stats/nb_records_per_gene_per_csq.tsv plot_oe_ratios Total mutation rate and number of variants per gene and consequence.

docs.title: dnm/
docs.text: File When Description dnms_kept.tsv dnm set DNMs kept after filtering on the gene list, coding regions, sex chromosomes and excluded regions. dnms_discarded.tsv dnm set DNMs removed by filtering, with the reason. dnms_annotated.tsv annotate_dnm Kept DNMs with their annotations. This is the file to pass as dnm to later runs.

docs.title: simulation/
docs.text:
One subdirectory per enrichment run type: all-coding/ and/or mis/.

File Description enrichment_results.tsv One row per gene with at least one observed DNM. See below. simulation_logs.json Per-gene details of the simulation. See below. batches/ Results for each batch of genes (symbolic links to the work directory).

docs.title: enrichment_results.tsv
docs.text: Column Description gene_id Gene identifier, as in the rates file. gene_symbol Gene symbol (if the rates file has a gene_symbol column). expected_score Expected gene score under the null model. observed_score Sum of the scores of the observed DNMs in the gene. p-value Probability of a gene score at least as high as the observed one under the null model.

docs.title: simulation_logs.json
docs.text:
A JSON object keyed by gene_id. For each gene:

Key Description nb_observed_dnms, nb_expected_dnms Number of observed DNMs and expected number of DNMs. observed_score, expected_score Observed and expected gene scores. expected_prob_per_consequence Expected number of DNMs per consequence. expected_score_per_consequence Contribution of each consequence to the expected score. nb_simulations, sequential_simulation, last_iteration_n How many simulations were run for the gene. info A note when the p-value was not simulated, e.g. observed < expected, pvalue set at 1. nb_missing_observed_scores, nb_missing_expected_scores, nb_missing_mutation_rate Variants with missing data. nb_rates_variants_imputed, nb_observed_variants_imputed, … Variants whose score was imputed or that were discarded (see impute_missing_scores). wall_time Time spent on the gene.

With debug = true, the log also contains the observed DNMs and the result of every simulation round.

docs.title: clustering/
docs.text:
One subdirectory per clustering run type: linear/, 3D/, and combined/ when runtype = "both".

Column Description gene_id, gene_symbol Gene identifiers. mutation_category Category of DNMs tested (missense, nonsense…). events_n Number of DNMs tested. dist Observed clustering distance. probability Clustering p-value. mode combined/ only: whether the result comes from the 3D or the linear test (3D is used when available).

docs.title: combined_tests/
docs.text:
Produced when the enrichment test runs with runtype = "both" and the clustering test also runs. combined_tests_results.tsv has one row per gene:

Column Description gene_id, gene_symbol Gene identifiers. min_pval Minimum of enrichment_all_pval and combined_mis_pval. This is the DeNovoWEST p-value. enrichment_all_pval Enrichment test p-value, all coding variants. combined_mis_pval Missense enrichment and clustering p-values combined with Fisher's method. enrichment_mis_pval Enrichment test p-value, missense variants. clustering_pval Clustering test p-value, missense variants. observed_all, expected_all Observed and expected gene scores, all coding variants. observed_mis, expected_mis Observed and expected gene scores, missense variants. clustering_nb_mis_variants, clustering_dist Number of missense DNMs and distance used by the clustering test. clustering_mode 3D or linear (clustering runtype = "both" only).

min_pval is the minimum of two tests, so correct for multiple testing accordingly: the 2020 publication used a Bonferroni threshold of 0.05 / (2 × number of genes tested). See Concepts.

docs.title: oe_ratios/
docs.text:
Produced when plot_oe_ratios = true.

File Description oe_ratios.json Observed / expected DNM ratio per consequence. oe_ratios_per_category.json Same, per gene category (if oe_ratios.gene_categories is set). oe_ratios_per_gnomad_loeuf_bins.json, oe_ratios_per_gnomad_missense_bins.json Same, per gnomAD constraint bin (if oe_ratios.gnomad_constraints is set). plots/*.png One plot per consequence and grouping.

docs.title: Outside outdir
docs.text: The example configuration files write Nextflow's execution timeline and resource report to ${basedir}/trace/${run_name}/. Intermediate files are in workDir and can be deleted once you no longer need to -resume the run.

docs.title: Workflow overview
docs.text:
The Nextflow workflow chains the steps of a DeNovoWEST analysis. Each step is switched on with a mode flag, so you can run everything at once or one step at a time, reusing earlier outputs.

flowchart TD
    subgraph rates [Rates]
        GFF[GFF + FASTA] --> CR[create_rates]
        CR --> AR[annotate_rates]
        RF[(rates)] -.existing file.-> AR
        AR --> FR[region filtering<br/>sperm adjustment]
    end
    subgraph dnm [DNMs]
        D[(dnm)] --> FD[gene, CDS, region<br/>and sex chromosome filtering]
        FD --> AD[annotate_dnm]
    end
    FR --> E[run_enrichment]
    AD --> E
    AD --> C[run_clustering]
    FR -.rates VCF.-> C
    E --> CMB[combined tests]
    C --> CMB
    FR --> OE[plot_oe_ratios]
    AD --> OE

docs.title: 1. Rates file creation (create_rates)
docs.text:
Lists every possible single-nucleotide substitution in the coding sequence and splice regions of each gene in the GFF, and assigns it an expected mutation rate from a mutation rate model (trinucleotide kmer, Roulette or Carlson). See Mutation rates.

Skip this step by giving an existing rates file with rates.

docs.title: 2. Annotation (annotate_rates, annotate_dnm)
docs.text:
Adds the same annotations to the rates file and the DNM file:

  • the predicted consequence of each variant (bcftools csq), used to select variants for each test;
  • one or more variant scores (CADD, dbNSFP scores such as AlphaMissense or REVEL, popEVE…), one of which is used as the severity score by the enrichment test;
  • gene-level information such as constraint metrics.

Then, for the rates file:

  • variants in excluded_regions are removed;
  • mutation rates can be adjusted for genes under positive selection in the male germline (sperm_positive_selection_adjustment);
  • a VCF version of the rates is written, which the clustering test can use.

docs.title: 3. DNM filtering
docs.text: Before annotation, DNMs are kept only if they fall in a gene of the gene list and in its coding sequence or splice region. DNMs in excluded_regions and, optionally, on sex chromosomes are removed. Discarded DNMs are written to dnm/dnms_discarded.tsv with the reason.

docs.title: 4. Enrichment test (run_enrichment)
docs.text: For each gene, compares the sum of the scores of the observed DNMs with its distribution under the null hypothesis, obtained by simulation from the rates file. Run on all coding variants, on missense variants only, or both. See Enrichment test.

docs.title: 5. Clustering test (run_clustering)
docs.text: Tests whether missense DNMs cluster along the protein sequence (linear) or in the predicted 3D structure (3D), using denovonear. See Clustering test.

docs.title: 6. Combined tests
docs.text: When both tests run (with enrichment runtype = "both"), the missense enrichment and clustering p-values are combined, and the minimum of this combined p-value and the all-coding enrichment p-value is reported for each gene. See Concepts.

docs.title: 7. Quality control (plot_oe_ratios)
docs.text: Compares observed and expected numbers of DNMs per consequence, overall and per gene category, to check that the mutation rate model is calibrated for your cohort.

docs.title: Parallelisation
docs.text: Genes are split into batches of split_step genes (default 100). Rates creation, annotation, enrichment and clustering run as one job per batch, and the results are merged at the end of each step.

docs.title: Typical ways of running it
docs.text:
Goal Modes Inputs Everything from scratch all gff, genome_fasta, dnm, rates_creation, annotation, enrichment, clustering Build an annotated rates file once, for several cohorts create_rates, annotate_rates gff, genome_fasta, rates_creation, annotation Analyse a new cohort with an existing rates file annotate_dnm, run_enrichment, run_clustering rates, dnm, gff, genome_fasta, annotation, enrichment, clustering Try other enrichment settings run_enrichment annotated rates and dnm from a previous run

See Recipes for complete examples.

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text: Each recipe shows the params block for a common analysis. Combine it with the header described in Configuration reference.

docs.title: Build an annotated rates file once
docs.text:
Building and annotating the rates file for all genes is the most expensive step. Do it once, then reuse the result for every cohort and enrichment setting.

params {
  create_rates = true
  annotate_rates = true

  gff = "/data/MANE.GRCh38.v1.0.ensembl_genomic.gff3.gz"
  genome_fasta = "/data/GRCh38.fa"
  excluded_regions = "/data/excluded_regions.bed"

  rates_creation {
    model = "kmer"
    path = "../resources/rates_model_dnn.tsv"
  }

  annotation {
    cadd_file = "/data/cadd/whole_genome_SNVs.tsv.gz"
    dbnsfp = [
      database: "/data/dbNSFP5.3.1a_grch38.gz",
      columns: "AlphaMissense_score,REVEL_score"
    ]
  }
}

The result is rates/merged_rates.tsv.gz (and rates/rates_adjusted.vcf.gz for clustering).

docs.title: Analyse a cohort with an existing rates file
docs.text:
params {
  annotate_dnm = true
  run_enrichment = true
  run_clustering = true

  rates = "/analyses/out/rates_kmer/rates/merged_rates.tsv.gz"
  dnm = "/data/cohort_dnms.tsv"
  gff = "/data/MANE.GRCh38.v1.0.ensembl_genomic.gff3.gz"
  genome_fasta = "/data/GRCh38.fa"
  excluded_regions = "/data/excluded_regions.bed"

  // Same sources as for the rates file, so that the DNMs get the same columns
  annotation {
    cadd_file = "/data/cadd/whole_genome_SNVs.tsv.gz"
    dbnsfp = [
      database: "/data/dbNSFP5.3.1a_grch38.gz",
      columns: "AlphaMissense_score,REVEL_score"
    ]
  }

  enrichment {
    nmales = 17422
    nfemales = 13636
    score = ["score", "AlphaMissense_score"]   // CADD for all coding, AlphaMissense for missense
    runtype = "both"
    cpus = 4
  }

  clustering {
    runtype = "both"
    protein_structures = "/data/alphafold/UP000005640_9606_HUMAN_v4.tar"
    rates = "/analyses/out/rates_kmer/rates/rates_adjusted.vcf.gz"
  }
}

Important

Annotate the DNMs with the same sources as the rates file. The enrichment test reads the score from the same column in both files.

docs.title: Use the Roulette mutation rate model
docs.text:
params {
  create_rates = true
  annotate_rates = true

  rates_creation {
    model = "roulette"
    path = "/data/roulette/"     // directory of per-chromosome Roulette VCFs
    scaling_factor = 5.075e-8    // required: default factor, or calibrate it on your cohort (see Mutation rates)
  }
  // ...
}

Use the Roulette rates in the clustering test too, with clustering.rates.

docs.title: Compare several settings
docs.text:
Keep basedir and change run_name for each setting, then compare the enrichment_results.tsv files:

params.basedir = "/analyses/cohort_2026"
params.run_name = "alphamissense_imputed"

params {
  run_enrichment = true
  rates = "/analyses/cohort_2026/out/annotation/rates/merged_rates.tsv.gz"
  dnm = "/analyses/cohort_2026/out/annotation/dnm/dnms_annotated.tsv"

  enrichment {
    nmales = 17422
    nfemales = 13636
    score = "AlphaMissense_score"
    runtype = "mis"
    impute_missing_scores = true
  }
}

docs.title: Test a configuration quickly
docs.text:
Before a full run, check your configuration on a few genes with few simulations:

params {
  gene_list = "my_10_genes.tsv"
  enrichment {
    nsim = 10000
    // ...
  }
}

docs.title: Reproduce a run exactly
docs.text: The enrichment test draws random numbers, so p-values vary slightly between runs. Set debug = true and cpus = 1 in enrichment to use a fixed seed. This also writes much more detailed logs, so only use it on a subset of genes.

docs.title: Run a single step without Nextflow
docs.text:
Every step of the workflow is also a command-line tool, for example:

denovowest simulation --nmales 17422 --nfemales 13636 --runtype mis \
    dnms_annotated.tsv merged_rates.tsv.gz AlphaMissense_score
